messages:
maya_support: opening thread for an escalation — ACME reports EventSource streams dropping in Safari behind Cloudflare. They see short connections ~20-90s then reconnects that sometimes deliver duplicated partial payloads. They only started after enabling edge caching for API paths.

customer-ACME: reproducer: Safari 15/16 on macOS, native EventSource to https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?token=TOKEN123. Behaviour: connects, receives some events, then connection closes. Client auto-reconnects and occasionally receives a truncated event or a duplicate chunk. Chrome shows steady stream, no duplicates.

maya_support: can you paste the network trace / response headers? suspect CDN revalidation (304) or incorrect cache headers.

customer-ACME: attached HAR snippets. Key piece shown from edge: 
HTTP/2 304 Not Modified
date: Mon, 19 May 2025 09:12:01 GMT
server: cloudflare
cf-cache-status: REVALIDATED
etag: "stream-v1-xyz"
cache-control: max-age=0
connection: keep-alive

(note: 304 has no body)

evan_frontend: okay 304 for an SSE route is effectively a connection cutoff from the client's POV. EventSource expects a 200 with an open chunked body. When edge returns 304 the browser sees stream ended. Different browsers handle this differently; Chrome appears more tolerant, Safari less so.

sam_engineer: recommended immediate mitigations for the customer:
- Bypass caching for SSE route at CDN (page rule or equivalent).
- On origin, add headers to prevent edge revalidation: `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` and/or `Surrogate-Control: no-store`.
- Include `X-Accel-Buffering: no` / `Cache-Control: no-transform` to try to keep proxies from buffering.

maya_support: customer also said they tried a polyfill (eventsource-polyfill) which switched to XHR streaming and then hit CORS credential issues. Polyfill behavior differs (sends cookies/auth) and requires `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` plus a specific `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` rather than `*`.

katie_sre: Cloudflare specifics: we should ask them to set a bypass for `/v1/stream*` and disable features that revalidate (like Origin Cache Control if misconfigured). Also watch for `CF-Cache-Status: HIT/REVALIDATED/EXPIRED`. If revalidation occurs, edge will send If-None-Match to origin and may reply 304 to client which breaks streaming.

customer-ACME: reproduced locally with curl and Cloudflare dev domain. `curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://edge.dev/v1/stream?token=..."` shows sometimes 200 with chunked body, sometimes 304. Safari always sees disconnect when 304 happens.

sam_engineer: server-side best-practice SSE headers we recommend (copy/paste):
```
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
X-Accel-Buffering: no
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.acme.example
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true   # only if using cookies or polyfill/XHR
```

sam_engineer: additional guidance on duplicates/partial events:
- Use SSE `id:` lines for every logical message. When EventSource reconnects, the browser sends `Last-Event-ID`. Server should honor that and resume from the next id, not resend the same id.
- Avoid splitting a single JSON object across multiple `data:` frames unless the client knows how to reassemble. Prefer one complete `data:` block per event.

maya_support: provided quick repro commands to customer:
1) `curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?token=TOKEN"` to observe if edge returns 200 chunked vs 304.
2) check `If-None-Match` requests and origin logs for `res.write("data: ...\\n\\n")` frequency.

customer-ACME: they applied `Surrogate-Control: no-store` and `Cache-Control: no-store` on origin and created a Cloudflare page rule to bypass cache for `/v1/stream*`. After that Safari was stable in a 2-hour soak test but they observed one reconnect that delivered the same chunk twice.

sam_engineer: for duplicate chunk prevention: implement server-side event id bookkeeping and check `Last-Event-ID` header sent by the client on reconnect. Example SSE envelope we recommend: 
```
id: 20250519-0001
event: delta
data: {"seq":42,"chunk":"..."}

```
Server should keep short-lived history of recent ids per connection and skip re-sending those ids.

evan_frontend: note about Safari quirks: if any intermediary adds `Content-Length` or sets `Connection: close` or returns a 3xx/304, Safari will often treat the stream as finished and reopen. There are also bugs around long-lived idle connections that require occasional keepalive comments (`: keepalive\n\n`) sent every ~15-30s to prevent some proxies/browsers from closing idle streams.

maya_support: customer asked about fallback strategies. Options:
- WebSocket fallback for browsers where SSE is flaky.
- Short-lived polling as a last resort.
- Polyfill with XHR streaming but ensure CORS and credentials are configured (and expect different behavior).

katie_sre: action items for internal follow-up:
- Add SSE CDN/Cloudflare checklist to our KB with recommended headers and page-rule examples.
- Add `curl -N` streaming check to smoke tests that exercises `/v1/stream` through our staging CDN config and fails if 304 observed.
- Add runtime alert for unexpected 3xx/304 on streaming endpoints.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging-disable-stream-cache -> 2025-05-19T14:00:00Z

maya_support: updated ticket with steps we asked ACME to try and requested prod rollout verification. Customer replied :thumbsup: and will monitor.

sam_engineer: I'll follow up with a quick PR adding SSE headers and id resume demo to our docs repo, and add a unit to runtime smoke test to `curl -N` through Cloudflare staging.

maria_notes: (internal) remember to document polyfill caveats: XHR approach triggers preflight and must use `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` if cookies/Authorization headers are sent. Also mention `EventSource` cannot set custom headers, so recommend token-in-query or cookie + CORS.

maya_support: closing internal thread once ACME confirms prod. leaving this thread as KB seed for "SSE + CDN + Safari".
